summary: Eight-row paged item list used by the bag/equipment/shop menus: resolves each visible row's item record, icon and count text, and tracks the page index and the per-row state mask.
evidence: Ui_ItemRows_MovePage (0x002FBA14) stores the page index at +0x50; Ui_ItemRows_RefreshRows (0x002FBC28) is the per-frame row fill; polymorphic (vtable calls at *self+0x3C/0x58/0x60/0x64/0x68) but the vtable itself is not in the batch.

fields.name: maybe_countSource
fields.evidence: self[0x0E] is dereferenced for a u16 at +0xC (count): MovePage compares it with 0x13 and uses f_c + page*8 - visibleRowCount for the scroll clamp; same pattern as Ui_PagedIconSelect.

fields.name: pageIndex
fields.evidence: MovePage keeps the page in self[0x14] ('if (param_1[0x14] != param_2) { param_1[0x14] = param_2; }') and computes pageCount as (vtable+0x64 rowCount - 1) / 8.

fields.name: partContext
fields.evidence: self[0x15] is the first argument of Ui_Part_GetAnimState (0x00647A88), Ui_Part_IsRecordSuppressedForMember (0x00646060), func_006479CC and maybe_Ui_Plate_FormatFullDescriptor in RefreshRows.

fields.name: itemIds
fields.evidence: self[0x16] is read as a u16 array: '*(u16 *)(self[0x16] + iVar16 * 2)' supplies each row's item id, and RefreshRows uses '*(u16 *)(self + 10) << 16 | 3 + i' pane ids for them.

fields.name: itemIdsEnd
fields.evidence: self[0x17] is the end of the same u16 array: RefreshRows tests 'iVar16 < iVar12 - iVar11 >> 1' with iVar11 = self[0x16], iVar12 = self[0x17].

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot3C
fields.evidence: No memory access at +0xF0. The evidence line '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x3c))(...)' is a vtable call; struct_db scaled the slot byte offset 0x3C by 4 to get 0xF0. Extraction artifact, not a field.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot58
fields.evidence: No memory access at +0x160. Evidence is a call through *param_1 + 0x58; 0x58 * 4 = 0x160 is a struct_db scale artifact.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot60
fields.evidence: No memory access at +0x180. Evidence is a call through *param_1 + 0x60; 0x60 * 4 = 0x180 is a struct_db scale artifact.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot68
fields.evidence: No memory access at +0x1A0. Evidence is a call through *param_1 + 0x68; 0x68 * 4 = 0x1A0 is a struct_db scale artifact.

fields.name: maybe_rowStateMask
fields.evidence: RefreshRows reads self[0xE2] once before the row loop and tests its low byte as a bit mask against the per-row anim state: '-(int)(char)iVar9 & uiPartGetAnimState', '(int)(char)iVar9 & uiPartIsRecordSuppressedForMember'.

summary: 12-byte init-only record allocated nowhere in the recovered call graph: it zeroes four bytes, stores 0x7F and 0x40, and is immediately followed by the 0xFE-byte path buffer written by Str_CopyDirectoryPath. The generated name is unsupported - the data looks like a file/stream descriptor, not a text colour range.
evidence: maybe_Sound_ChannelParams_Init (0x00542910) sits between Snd_InitStreamSlot (0x005428EC) and Str_CopyDirectoryPath (0x00542964), both of which operate on the same fs/stream block; no callers. IMPORTANT: struct_db indexed the body as u32* but the ARM body uses strb, so every batch offset here is 4x the real byte offset (see each field).

fields.name: unknown_byte0
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4]' = byte offset 0. struct_db reported 0 only by coincidence; real size is one byte, not four.

fields.name: unknown_byte1
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #1]' = byte offset 1; the batch offset 4 is 4x the true offset.

fields.name: unknown_byte2
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #2]' = byte offset 2; batch offset 8 = 4x.

fields.name: unknown_byte3
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #3]' = byte offset 3; batch offset 12 = 4x.

fields.name: maybe_volume
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r0, [r4, #4]' with r0 = 0x7F (127) - the classic 3DS volume scale. Batch offset 16 = 4x the true byte 4.

fields.name: maybe_pan
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r1, [r4, #7]' with r1 = 0x40 (64, centre) - a 0..127 pan pair with the 0x7F above. Batch offset 28 = 4x the true byte 7.

fields.name: unknown_byte8
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #8]' = byte 8; batch offset 32 = 4x.

fields.name: unknown_byte9
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #9]' = byte 9; batch offset 36 = 4x.

fields.name: unknown_byte10
fields.evidence: Real write is 'strb r5, [r4, #0xA]' = byte 10; batch offset 40 = 4x.

fields.name: unknown_byte11
fields.evidence: Real target is byte 11: 'func_00111384(self + 0xB, 2, 0xFFFFFFFF)' fills 2 bytes 0xFF there; 'strh r5, [r4, #5]' clears the u16 at byte 5. Batch offset 44 = 4x the true byte 11.

summary: Title-screen attract demo: owns a Ui handle set, the demo player/sequence handles and three embedded animation nodes, and restarts itself when the player reports the demo finished.
evidence: Ui_TitleDemo_Init (0x001F1628) builds three embedded 0x20-spaced animation nodes and a 0xDE4-byte player; Ui_TitleDemo_Update (0x001F1B04) validates the handle set at +0x1C, restarts on func_00636EC8()!=0 and releases the handles at +0x54/+0x58 and the three nodes.

fields.name: unknown_gameWorkTemp
fields.evidence: No store to self+0: the write in Ui_TitleDemo_Init ('*puVar5 = extraout_r1') targets the Game_GetWork return buffer, then '*puVar8 = puVar5' writes self+0x131. Extraction artifact.

fields.name: handleSet
fields.evidence: Ui_HandleSet_ValidateAndConvert(&self->f_1C) in Ui_TitleDemo_Update; the handle set is embedded at +0x1C (UiHandleSet is listed as 60 bytes in structs.json but the next demo fields are at +0x54, so only the head is proven).

fields.name: handleSetValidated
fields.evidence: 'if (self->f_1D == '\0') { Ui_HandleSet_ValidateAndConvert(&self->f_1C); }' - second byte of the embedded handle set acts as the 'already converted' flag.

fields.name: playerHandle
fields.evidence: Ui_TitleDemo_Update tests self->f_54 as the 'demo running' gate and frees it through func_0021F8B8(Ui_GetCore()->f_C, self->f_54) on restart; the doc names the two demo player handles at +0x54/+0x58.

fields.name: sequenceHandle
fields.evidence: Freed by the same func_0021F8B8 UI-core release right after +0x54, then zeroed; the second of the two demo player handles.

fields.name: animNode0
fields.evidence: Embedded node at +0x5C with its own vtable: 'if (self->f_6C) { (**(code **)(self->f_5C + 8))((int *)&self->f_5C); self->f_6C = 0; }' - first of three 0x20-spaced anim nodes built by Ui_TitleDemo_Init.

fields.name: hasAnimNode0
fields.evidence: Flag paired with the +0x5C node: set means the node is alive and must be released through its vtable slot +8, then cleared.

fields.name: animNode1
fields.evidence: Second embedded node at +0x7C, released the same way ('(**(code **)(self->f_7C + 8))(&self->f_7C)') when its flag +0x8C is set.

fields.name: hasAnimNode1
fields.evidence: 'if (self->f_8C != '\0') { (**(code **)(self->f_7C + 8))(...); self->f_8C = 0; }' - alive flag of the second anim node.

fields.name: animNode2
fields.evidence: Third embedded node at +0xB8, released through its vtable slot +8 in Ui_TitleDemo_Update; its alive flag is the byte at +0xC8 ('*(char *)(self + 200)'), just outside the batch offsets.

summary: Layout (BFLAN) animation binder: keeps the animation group, the playhead time, the animatable-target array and a fixed array of (pane, tag) bindings that it samples every frame.
evidence: Ui_Animator_AppendBinding (0x00536C48) fills self+0x1C with 8-byte (target, tag) pairs up to capacity self+0x22; Ui_Animator_ApplyTagData (0x00536E78) samples them at self+0x10; vtable 0x0072FB2C slots 2..4 dispatch to target layout objects.

fields.name: animGroup
fields.evidence: Ui_Animator_BindByName reads group = self->f_C, then group->f_E (entry count) and group->f_10 (entry offset table, stride 4) and matches each entry name against pane+0x80.

fields.name: frameTime
fields.evidence: 'fVar25 = *(float *)(param_1 + 0x10)' is the keyframe time compared against the tag curves in Ui_Animator_ApplyTagData (the same value is passed to 0x0053779C as the current frame).

fields.name: maybe_animResourceId
fields.evidence: ReleaseBindings calls 'func_00534BF4(self, self->f_14, self->f_2C->f_34 >> 2)' - an id/index of the animation resource rebuilt together with the binding table.

fields.name: animatableObjects
fields.evidence: self->f_18 is a pointer array checked as '*(int *)(*(int *)(self->f_18 + i * 4) + 0x10) == 0' while validating a tag, and AppendBinding rejects the tag when self->f_18 is null.

fields.name: bindings
fields.evidence: Field writes are 'piVar7 = (int *)(self->f_1C + (u32)f20 * 8); *piVar7 = target; piVar7[1] = tag;' - the (pane, tag) binding array.

fields.name: bindingCount
fields.evidence: Incremented once per appended binding: 'uVar2 = *(ushort *)(param_1 + 0x20); *(ushort *)(param_1 + 0x20) = uVar2 + 1;' and used as the array index.

fields.name: bindingCapacity
fields.evidence: Guard at the top of AppendBinding/BindByName: 'if ((u32)self->f_22 <= (u32)f20) return 0;' - maximum number of (pane, tag) pairs.

fields.name: animTransform
fields.evidence: ReleaseBindings dereferences self->f_2C for a flag word (+0x40, bit 1 = active, bit 2 = busy), a count at +0x34>>2 and then zeroes self->f_2C; the object that owns the sampled transform state.

fields.name: layout
fields.evidence: self->f_30 exposes a pane-pointer array (*f_30) with a u16 count at +4, a material array at +0x3C and a material count at +0x40, walked by ReleaseBindings to clear pane transforms.

summary: Screen-slide (push) transition: stores the target pane, its child parts and their X offsets and slides them in three states (out, hold 0.4 s, in) at +/-400 px/s.
evidence: Ui_ScreenSlideAnim_Start (0x004F06A4) caches the target offset and every child's +0x9C into arrays; Ui_ScreenSlideAnim_Update (0x004F08F8) implements the 3 states with the exact constants -400.0/400.0/0.4; ApplyPartOffset pushes self->f_68 to the target and the +0x6C array to the children.

fields.name: targetPane

fields.name: childParts

fields.name: childCount

fields.name: holdTimer

fields.name: targetOffset

fields.name: currentOffset

fields.name: childOffsets

summary: Seven-row paged selector: keeps the row cursor/entry count and an embedded text-list model, and rebinds the seven rows when the page changes. Its 436-byte field set is byte-for-byte the Ui_TextListWindow layout.
evidence: Ui_SevenRowSelector_Scroll (0x00477D04) clears/rebinds seven 8-byte row slots at +0x70 and clamps the cursor with /7 %7; Ui_SevenRowSelector_SelectRow (0x00477F70) resolves the record from the table at +0xAC, calls Container_SetCountFromByteSize/Ui_TextListWindow_UpdateItemRects on the embedded window at +0x54 and Ui_List_SelectEntryById on the list at +0x38.

fields.name: paneGroupId

fields.name: list

fields.name: entryCount

evidence: Ui_SlotMachineDisplay_Dtor (0x0039364C): calls the owner hook at +0x98, Casino_Slot_UpdateSpinState(&self+0x120), then func_004C340C(&self+0xEC0/0x1064/0x1208/0x13AC/0x1550/0x16F4, &self+0x220) - the six reels with a 0x1A4 stride; the same function set names the class Casino_Slot in structs.json.
